bimi-svg-validator.quickAnswer: BIMI (Brand Indicators for Message Identification) lets verified brands show their logo in email inboxes, but the SVG logo must follow strict rules. Paste your SVG or upload the file and this tool checks every rule locally: well-formed XML, square viewBox, a title element, no scripts, no event handlers, no external references, and size under 32KB.
keyFacts: BIMI displays brand logos next to authenticated emails in supporting inboxes like Gmail and Apple Mail.
The logo must be SVG Tiny 1.2 (Tiny-PS): a restricted, secure SVG profile.
BIMI requires a square canvas and recommends keeping the file under 32KB.
A <title> element is required; it provides the accessible name of the logo.
Scripts, event handlers, external references, and embedded fonts are all forbidden.
howTo: Paste your SVG markup or upload the .svg file.
Read the pass/fail result for each BIMI rule.
Fix any failing rule in your SVG editor.
Re-paste and re-check until all checks pass.
Only then publish the SVG at your BIMI record URL.
bimi-svg-validator.formula:
BIMI SVG rules checked:
1. Well-formed XML, root <svg>
2. viewBox present and square (1:1 ratio)
3. <title> element present
4. No <script>, no on* handlers, no <foreignObject>
5. No external href or url() references
6. File size <= 32KB (32768 bytes)

faqs.a: Brand Indicators for Message Identification: a standard that lets authenticated brands display their logo beside emails in supporting inboxes.

faqs.q: Why must the logo be square?
faqs.a: Inbox providers render BIMI logos in square slots. A non-square logo would be cropped or distorted, so the spec requires a 1:1 canvas.
Email clients must never execute code from a logo. Scripts, event handlers, and external references are attack vectors, so BIMI bans them.
BIMI guidance recommends keeping the SVG under 32KB so it loads fast and cannot hide malicious payloads. Larger files risk rejection.

faqs.q: Does passing here guarantee my logo shows?
faqs.a: No. You also need DMARC enforcement, a published BIMI DNS record, and (for Gmail) a Verified Mark Certificate. This tool only validates the SVG file.
